details: Japanese financial giant SBI Group, in partnership with Visa, has launched new crypto reward cards. These cards convert spending points into Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), or XRP, with Gold card users able to earn up to 10% in crypto rewards during a promotional campaign. This initiative aims to integrate everyday payments with crypto accumulation.
title: SBI Group & Visa Launch Crypto Card with BTC, ETH, XRP Rewards

details: Coinbase Global Inc. has announced a breakthrough agreement regarding stablecoin yield provisions, potentially ending a legislative stalemate in the U.S. Senate. The compromise addresses a contentious "rewards" feature that had previously stalled progress on digital asset market structure legislation, protecting the right of American users to earn rewards and clearing a path for a broader crypto bill.
title: Coinbase Compromise Paves Way for US Stablecoin Bill

details: Bitcoin's Cumulative Volume Delta (CVD) indicator has surged by 199.1% over the past week, with spot CVD rising significantly. This indicates aggressive buying in the spot market. Institutional inflows to Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs), particularly BlackRock's IBIT, have re-accelerated, providing support for Bitcoin's price above the $78,000 level.
title: Bitcoin Spot CVD Surges 199% Amid Institutional Inflows

details: Ripple has expanded its banking footprint in Korea through a custody deal with Kbank. This development signifies increased adoption of Ripple's solutions within the traditional financial sector in South Korea, potentially leading to greater utility for XRP.
title: Ripple Expands Korean Banking with Kbank Custody Deal

details: Polygon (POL) saw an increase after Visa integrated it into its global stablecoin settlement program on April 29, 2026. This integration is anticipated to boost stablecoin volume and transaction fees on the Polygon network, highlighting a growing mainstream adoption for blockchain infrastructure in traditional finance.
title: Polygon Gains as Visa Integrates for Stablecoin Settlement

details: Tether, the issuer of the USDT stablecoin, slowed its gold purchases to 6 tons in the first quarter of 2026. As of March 31, gold represented 10% ($19.8 billion) of Tether's reserves, which are predominantly composed of U.S. Treasury Bills ($117 billion).
title: Tether Slows Gold Purchases in Q1
